correctness.rationale: The open N(u) subset N(v) fold deletes v by independence-complex dominated-vertex equivalence; the closed N[u] subset N[v] split gives a wedge with a suspended deletion of N[v] because u cones off the attaching link. The 15 actual prefix-mask rules specify valid u,v and exact normalized children, and all tested neighborhoods involve only the first four rows because edges have longitudinal range one; the identities therefore extend to any complete-row tail. I independently reimplemented graph masks and verified 119 template instances for tail lengths 2..9, together with exact recursive open/closed reduction of X1..X5 yielding p1=z, p2=z+2z², p3=3z², p4=z²+4z³, p5=5z³+4z⁴. The template equations imply X_n ≃ ΣX_(n-2) ∨2Σ²X_(n-3) for n>=6; induction gives all sphere wedges and torsion-free integral homology. Under the halfturn all two-vertex opposite-column orbits are independent; a fixed simplex barycentric assignment is equivalent to choosing conflict-free orbit classes, exactly Ind(P_n boxtimes P2). The rectangular P2 prior recurrence has identical TOTAL mod2 Betti numbers, giving equality in Smith inequality for every n. Finite local tests support but never substitute for the locality argument and induction.
